solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Succeed in kidnap

definitions.meaning: to succeed at something, like winning a prize, is to manage it with style
to kidnap someone is to abduct them or take them away by force

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb has two senses: winning or managing something well, and taking a person away by force.

clue.text: I mean to play cartoon

indicators.note: letters set to play are tossed about freely, so these two words get rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone explains that they intend to put on a cartoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to play' rearranges the five letters of I MEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Japanese animation is a style of cartoon, often in film or television series.

clue.text: Share offer of legal entitlement to succeed children

parts.note: a legal entitlement is a right
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees and lists of monarchs
issue is a formal word for a person's children or offspring

explanation.surface: An offer of shares sets out a legal right for children to inherit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'succeed' looks like part of an inheritance story; it is only the letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: A company makes this kind of issue when it offers new shares to its existing shareholders.

clue.text: We ought, I suspect, to be more important

indicators.note: something suspect is dubious and not to be trusted as it stands, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A speaker guesses that some duty of theirs ought to take priority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' looks like 'I think', but it rearranges WE OUGHT plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: To outweigh something is to be greater in significance or value than it.

clue.text: Time so unheard of in new interpretation (after Albert Einstein originally abstracted)

definitions.text: Time so unheard of in new interpretation (after Albert Einstein originally abstracted)

indicators.note: a new interpretation of the letters puts them in a fresh order, so the words before it are rearranged
originally picks the first letter of each name, and abstracted says those letters are taken away from the pool

explanation.surface: Einstein came up with a startlingly new interpretation of time.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of TIME SO UNHEARD OF IN, take away A and E (the first letters of Albert and Einstein, as 'originally abstracted' says), and rearrange what is left. The whole clue is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In relativity, time is treated as an extra dimension added to the three of space.

clue.text: Skim inside iced nougat topping

indicators.note: inside says one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: glacé means iced or candied, as in glacé cherries

indicators.note: the topping of a word is its first letter, here of nougat

explanation.surface: Someone skims the icing on top of a sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts N, the first letter of nougat ('topping'), into GLACE.
explanation.definitionFit: To glance through a text is to read it quickly, the same as skimming it.

clue.text: Windows, perhaps, on sailor's instrument

parts.note: Microsoft Windows is an example of a GUI, a graphical user interface
tar is an old name for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor plays an instrument while looking out of the windows.
explanation.walkthrough: GUI stands for graphical user interface, and Windows is one; 'on' just puts it before TAR.
explanation.definitionFit: This stringed instrument is played by plucking or strumming.

clue.text: Half of guinea-pig went past

indicators.note: half of the word means its first three letters out of six are kept

parts.note: the agouti is a South American rodent closely related to the guinea pig, and agouti also names the guinea pig's wild-type coat

explanation.surface: Half of a guinea pig wandered off.
explanation.walkthrough: The rodent stands for AGOUTI, a close relative of the guinea pig; 'Half of' keeps the first three letters. 'went' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means gone by, as in 'ten years past' meaning ten years before now.

clue.text: Captain's chest contains gold

indicators.note: contains says the first piece holds the second within it

parts.note: a commode is a chest of drawers
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A ship's captain keeps gold in his sea chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Captain' is a loose definition: this naval rank sits just above captain, and a commode here is furniture, not a ship's sea chest.
explanation.definitionFit: This naval officer commands a group of ships, a rank above a ship's captain.

clue.text: With passport, possibly obtain object

parts.note: a passport is one example of ID, a proof of identity
to obtain is to get

explanation.surface: With a passport you might obtain something.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an informal word for a small gadget or object whose name you do not know.

clue.text: Maybe suits college applications?

parts.note: uni is short for university, a college
applications are made on forms

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether college application paperwork suits them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suits' looks like a verb, but it means sets of matching clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Suits of matching clothes worn by staff are one example of standard dress.

clue.text: Twisted passion

definitions.meaning: twisted means ... out of shape, or crooked and dishonest
a passion for something is a strong natural inclination towards it

explanation.definitionFit: The word means crooked or out of shape, and as a noun a natural talent or leaning.

clue.text: Pulling former girlfriend first for breeding

indicators.note: first says this piece comes ahead of the one before it in the clue

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
traction is the act of pulling

explanation.surface: A man is pulling his ex-girlfriend first for the sake of breeding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulling' looks like the definition, but it gives TRACTION; 'first' puts EX ahead of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's extraction is their family descent or ancestry, a sense close to their breeding.

clue.text: Demanding viva to obtain doctorate, possibly?

definitions.meaning: a demanding viva is a gruelling oral examination, a harsh questioning
after a bachelor's and a master's degree

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for hard interrogation, and literally it is the degree that comes after two others.

clue.text: Cut a bold bank down

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bold, as in typefaces and pencils
a ridge is a raised strip of ground, a bank

explanation.surface: Someone cuts a steep bank down to size.
explanation.definitionFit: A text that has been cut has been shortened, as an abridged edition is.

clue.text: One prints in black beneath hollow

indicators.note: in a down clue beneath puts this piece below the one after it

parts.note: a bubble is a hollow sphere of liquid
jet is a deep black colour

explanation.surface: A printer's work appears in black beneath a hollow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beneath' puts JET under BUBBLE in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a kind of inkjet printer, a machine that prints.

clue.text: Fraudster's confession to religious figure

parts.note: a fraudster admitting what they do would say 'I'
and the deed they admit is to con people

explanation.surface: A conman confesses his crimes to a religious figure.
explanation.walkthrough: A fraudster owning up says 'I con'.
explanation.definitionFit: An image of a saint or of Christ painted on wood is a religious figure of this kind.

clue.text: How to describe difficult crossword to crossword lover using English language, explaining some solving openings

indicators.note: openings are the first letters, here of each word from the second crossword to solving

parts.words: crossword lover using English language, explaining some solving

explanation.surface: A setter explains in English how to describe a hard puzzle to a crossword fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'openings' takes the first letter of each word from the second 'crossword' to 'solving'.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossword with no hints at all would be impossible, so it is fair to call it without clues.

clue.text: On Saturday, English Big Brother fades away

indicators.note: in an across clue on means the piece before is placed in front of the next

parts.note: BB is short for Big Brother, the TV show
S is short for Saturday

explanation.surface: Interest in the TV show Big Brother fades on a Saturday night.
explanation.walkthrough: Big Brother is a reality TV show, abbreviated BB.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide ebbs when it goes out, so the verb also means fades or declines.

clue.text: Fruit almost perishes in pleasant airs

indicators.note: almost says the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a melon is a fruit
to perish is to die

explanation.surface: A fruit is almost rotten while pleasant music plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Airs are tunes, and these are tunes that are pleasant to hear.

clue.text: Record very small amount of time

definitions.meaning: a written record of a meeting is called its ...
an amount of time of sixty seconds

explanation.definitionFit: The word, said two ways, means a meeting's record, a sixty-second span and a tiny size.

clue.text: Say splitting up marriage results in loyalty

indicators.note: splitting up says the piece before goes inside the word that follows

parts.note: an alliance can be a marriage between families
EG is short for exempli gratia, for example, so it stands for say

explanation.surface: Someone says that breaking up a marriage tests one's faithfulness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splitting up' reads like a divorce in the surface, but it is the container signal; 'results in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being loyal to a cause or ruler is pledging allegiance.

clue.text: Endlessly bewilder birds

indicators.note: endlessly says the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: to bemuse is to bewilder

explanation.surface: The birds are endlessly confusing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' drops the B and E from each end of BEMUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: These large flightless Australian birds are related to ostriches.

clue.text: Detach peacekeepers on exercise next to German capital

parts.note: UN peacekeepers belong to the United Nations
PE is physical education, exercise

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first letter, here of German

explanation.surface: Peacekeepers carry out an exercise near the German capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' takes the first letter of German; 'on' and 'next to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To take the peg off something releases or detaches it, as a currency from another.

clue.text: Spread jib out in part to get to country

indicators.note: part says only a portion of the words before it is used, the answer sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A sailor spreads the jib out to reach a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' hides the answer across spreaD JIB OUT In. 'Spread' looks like an anagram signal, but the letters are in order.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small country in the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: I disapprove of blunder sacrificing bishop

indicators.note: a sacrifice gives something up, so the bishop is removed

parts.note: a boob is a blunder
B is the abbreviation for bishop in chess

explanation.surface: A chess player admits a blunder in giving up a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the cry an audience makes to show it disapproves.

clue.text: Turned on bad parent

indicators.note: bad means the letters are spoilt and so put in a different order

explanation.surface: A bad parent is turned on by others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges PARENT. 'Turned on' looks like 'attacked', but means thrilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Being enraptured or delighted is being turned on in the sense of excited.

clue.text: Struggled to run furnace outside

indicators.note: outside says the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: a stove is a furnace or heater
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone struggled to run outside the furnace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps STOVE around R.
explanation.definitionFit: Strove is the past tense of strive, to struggle or try hard.

clue.text: Homes suppress urge to set aside funds

indicators.note: to suppress something is to hold it in, so the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: nests are homes for birds
to egg someone on is to urge them

explanation.surface: Homeowners resist the urge to save money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'urge' reads as a noun in the surface but is the verb, as in egging someone on.
explanation.definitionFit: Money saved for the future is this kind of reserve, funds put by.
